content: Indinavir increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Isoniazid increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Istradefylline increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Clinical trials have shown that istradefylline at 40 mg/day increases peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Consider dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the levels or effects of itraconazole by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both itraconazole and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Both ketoconazole and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Larotrectinib decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Both artemether/lumefantrine and lenvatinib prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Artemether/lumefantrine increases the levels or effects of loratadine by influencing hepatic CYP2D6 metabolism and decreases its levels or effects by affecting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Lorlatinib decreases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Both mavorixafor and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Mavorixafor causes concentration-dependent QTc prolongation. Monitor QTc during treatment in patients with risk factors for QTc prolongation, such as co-administered medications that increase mavorixafor exposure or other drugs with a high risk of QTc prolongation. Dose reduction or discontinuation of mavorixafor may be required. Mefloquine decreases the levels of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Mefloquine decreases bile production; Coartem (lumefantrine) should be taken with food. Mifepristone and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. Mitotane decreases the levels of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Mitotane is a strong inducer of cytochrome P450 3A4; monitor for possible dosage adjustments when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Both artemether/lumefantrine and ofloxacin prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both artemether/lumefantrine and olodaterol inhaled prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Drugs that prolong the QTc interval may potentiate the cardiovascular effects of beta-2 agonists, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Both osilodrostat and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Both osimertinib and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Conduct periodic monitoring with ECGs and electrolytes in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QTc interval. Oxaliplatin increases the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine through other mechanisms. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Monitor for ECG changes if therapy is initiated in patients taking drugs known to prolong the QT interval. Both ozanimod and artemether/lumefantrine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Due to potential additive effects on heart rate, treatment with ozanimod should generally not be initiated in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs with known arrhythmogenic properties. Both artemether/lumefantrine and paliperidone prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Both quetiapine and artemether/lumefantrine may increase each other's toxicity through QTc interval prolongation. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Avoid use with drugs that prolong QT and in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT interval. Postmarketing cases show QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or with drugs known to cause electrolyte imbalance or prolong QT. Both quizartinib and artemether/lumefantrine may increase each other's effects through QTc interval prolongation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Monitor patients more frequently with ECG if co-administered with QT-prolonging drugs. Both artemether/lumefantrine and ranolazine prolong the QTc interval. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Rilpivirine should be used with caution when co-administered with a drug with a known risk of Torsade de Pointes.
